observations: Two large eye-like forms dominate the upper half: the left is a concentric circle with radiating spokes in amber and white; the right is a rectangular form packed with dense parallel lines in black, pink, and blue.
A row of white rectangular tooth shapes runs across the lower third, overlaid with teal, magenta, and black scribbled lines against a dark ground.
A jagged magenta and yellow border frames the whole composition against a near-black field, with the artist's mark visible in the lower left corner.
reading: The two eye zones pull against each other: one built from rings that expand outward, the other from tight parallel bars that compress inward. That opposition gives the face an off-balance, wide-awake quality. The tooth row below reads as a grin or a grimace depending on how long you look. Warm amber and yellow at the center cool toward pink and teal at the edges, shifting the mood as the eye moves.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #43 and #45. Where #43 floats on an open blue field with scattered multicolor lines, #44 closes the background to near-black and concentrates color inside the face, making the forms feel more enclosed.

connections.reason: Both works use layered multicolor scribble lines over blocked face forms, but #43 spreads those lines across an open blue ground while #44 compresses them inside a dark-bordered enclosure, sharpening the contrast between inside and outside.

Both #44 and #45 show a wide tooth row in the lower section and concentric eye forms, but #45 uses a saturated red surround and squarer geometry where #44 uses a dark field and a rounder left eye, making the shared vocabulary visible across different color moods.

lookingQuestion: The left eye is built from expanding rings and the right from compressed parallel bars — what does that difference in line structure do to how you read the two sides of the face?
ambiguities: The nnotb #182 comparison image shows multiple small face forms across a busy field and shares a dark ground and warm palette, but no single formal element connects strongly enough to the primary work to warrant inclusion.
Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align here, but the metadata notes gaps may exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so sequence position should not be read as strict making order.
